Building reference and contaminant databases

Source: vignettes/building-databases.Rmd
building-databases.Rmd

metacleaner needs two sets of sequences besides the database you want to clean:

  • a reference set of the group you want to keep (e.g. all plant ITS1/ITS2 sequences in GenBank), and
  • a contaminant set of groups that should not be in your database (e.g. all non-plant ITS sequences).

build_reference_db() downloads these from NCBI and tidies them in one step: it keeps only the accession in each header, removes empty sequences and writes each sequence on a single line. Previously this took a mix of R, awk, perl, sed and seqkit commands.

These downloads need an internet connection and can take hours for large searches. Get a free NCBI API key (https://account.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) to make them about three times faster, and store it once per session:

Sys.setenv(ENTREZ_KEY = "your_key_here")

Plant ITS1/ITS2 example (Crone et al. 2023) 

library(metacleaner)

# Wanted: plant ITS1/5.8S/28S/ITS2 sequences
build_reference_db(
  term = '((((ITS1) OR 5.8S) OR 28S) OR ITS2) AND Embryophyta[Organism] AND ("0"[SLEN] : "10000"[SLEN])',
  file = "ITS_plants.fasta"
)

# Unwanted: the same markers from everything that is not a land plant
build_reference_db(
  term = '((((ITS1) OR 5.8S) OR 28S) OR ITS2) NOT Embryophyta[Organism] AND ("0"[SLEN] : "10000"[SLEN])',
  file = "ITS_nonplants.fasta",
  dereplicate = TRUE
)

The search term is written exactly as you would type it into the NCBI Nucleotide website, so you can test it there first and see how many records it returns.

If a download stops (for example because the connection dropped), run the same command again: it continues where it left off.

Should I remove duplicate sequences?

dereplicate = TRUE keeps only one copy of each distinct sequence. This is fine, and saves time, for the contaminant set. Do not dereplicate the reference set: if a sequence is shared by Malus and Pyrus, keeping only the Malus copy hides the ambiguity, and metacleaner can no longer flag a query as “matches multiple genus”.

Taxonomy

The easiest option is taxonomy = "ncbi" in clean_reference(). It looks up only the accessions that are needed. To avoid downloading them again in later runs, look them up once and save them:

ids <- c(names(read_fasta("my_database.fasta")),
         names(read_fasta("ITS_plants.fasta")))
tax <- taxonomy_from_ncbi(ids, cache = "taxonomy_cache.rds")
write.table(tax, "taxonomy_table.tsv", sep = "\t", row.names = FALSE, quote = FALSE)

You can then use taxonomy = "taxonomy_table.tsv". If you already have a local taxonomizr database, use taxonomy = "path/to/accessionTaxa.sql".

Doing the steps yourself 

download_ncbi_sequences("Malus[Organism] AND ITS2", "malus_raw.fasta")
seqs <- read_fasta("malus_raw.fasta")   # headers reduced to accessions
seqs <- dereplicate(seqs)               # optional
write_fasta(seqs, "malus.fasta")
